answer: A jury-bond Sybil defense: each agent identity locks a slashable bond, and every action touching shared state is co-signed by a rotating panel of bonded peers who each hold stake on the verdict. A fake cluster that only vouches for itself is a mirror of one actor, so a single challenge links them and slashes all bonds at once. To sway a vote, an attacker must fund hundreds of independent, separately drawn bonds — a flat mesa of cost with no refund after detection, while honest agents pay once. The honest tide of jurors dilutes any single stake.
